meaning: to do (casual); to work at a job

senses.en: to do (casual; very often in 干什么 'do what?')
to work; to do a job or a task (你是干什么的？ 'what do you do?')

examples.en: What are you doing?
examples.analysis: 干 is the verb 'do' and 什么 'what' is its object. The answer swaps 干什么 for the real activity: 我在吃饭 'I'm eating'. 在 before the verb marks an action in progress. 你在做什么？ means the same; 干 sounds more casual.

examples.en: What do you do for a living?
examples.analysis: 是 + 干什么 + 的 = 'someone who does what?': the 的 turns the activity into a kind of person, so this asks about a job, not about right now. Answer 我是医生. It is blunt: from a guard to a stranger it means 'who are you?'. In small talk, 你做什么工作？ is safer.

examples.en: This is too exhausting. I quit!
examples.analysis: 不 + 干 + 了 = 'not doing it any more': the final 了 marks a change, so the speaker is giving up a job or a task. Without 了, 我不干 is a flat refusal, 'I won't do it'.

collocations.en: capable; good at getting things done

related.en: to do; more neutral, and the verb in 做饭 'cook'
dry; a different entry (first tone), as in 干净 'clean'

meaning: plural suffix for pronouns and words for people (我们, 朋友们)

senses.en: makes pronouns plural: 我们 'we', 你们 'you (all)', 他们 'they'
after a noun for people: a known group (朋友们, 同学们)

examples.en: What would you all like to drink?
examples.analysis: 你 + 们 = 'you' for two or more people, as a host or a waiter asks a table. 们 is toneless and joins the pronoun into one word; the same move gives 我们 'we' and 他们 'they'. To one guest you would say 你想喝什么？

examples.en: Everyone, there's no class tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 同学们 is how a teacher addresses a whole class: 们 turns 同学 'classmate' into the group in front of you. Calling out to a group this way is common with 同学们 and 朋友们.

examples.zh: 朋友们都到了，我们吃饭吧。
examples.en: Our friends are all here, so let's eat.
examples.analysis: 朋友们 means a known group: the friends we were waiting for. 们 is not needed for every plural (我有很多朋友 has none), and standard Mandarin does not add it after a number: 三个朋友, not 三个朋友们.

collocations.en: friends (a known group; also how you address them)

related.en: some; after 这 / 那 / 哪 it makes a plural, for people or things: 这些人 'these people'
everybody; a common way to address a whole group (大家好)

hook: 亻 'person' + 门 mén for the sound: a suffix for people.

meaning: words; what someone says; speech

senses.en: words; what someone says (他的话 'what he said')
something to say (有话 'have something to say')
a language or dialect, in casual speech (中国话 'Chinese')

measure.note: 一句话 'one sentence; in a word'

examples.en: Who said that?
examples.analysis: 这话 = 'this remark' (what was just said). 是…的 picks out one detail of a past event, here who did the saying: 是谁说的 'who was it that said it'. 话 is the noun for spoken words; the verb is 说.

examples.en: If you've got something to say, just say it.
examples.analysis: 有话 = 'have something to say'. Two parts with no word for 'if': 有话 + 就 'then' + 说吧, where 就 links condition and result. You say it to someone who is hesitating; 吧 makes it an invitation.

examples.en: I'll remember what you said.
examples.analysis: 你的话 'your words' comes first as the topic, then the comment 我记住了 'I've got it fixed in memory'. Putting the object first like this is common in speech. The line promises you won't forget the advice.

meaning: thing; stuff; things (objects, food, belongings)

senses.en: thing; stuff (any object, often when you don't name it)
things to eat or buy (吃东西 'eat something', 买东西 'go shopping')
said of a person, a strong insult: 他不是东西 'he's a scoundrel (rude)'

measure.note: 一个东西; 件 jiàn is also common

examples.en: What is this thing?
examples.analysis: 什么东西 = 'what thing': 什么 sits right before a noun, like 'what' + noun in English. 东西 is the catch-all word when you don't know or don't need the name. Said with a frown, it means 'what is this stuff?'.

examples.en: Did you eat anything this morning?
examples.analysis: 吃东西 = 'eat something', with no particular food in mind: here 东西 means food. 了 + 吗 asks whether it happened. A doctor or a parent asks exactly this; 吃饭 would sound more like 'have a meal'.

examples.en: Don't forget your things.
examples.analysis: 你的东西 = 'your stuff': bag, phone, keys. 别忘了 'don't forget' is the usual form, with 了 right after 忘. Mind the tone: dōngxi with toneless xi is 'thing'; dōngxī with first tone means 'east and west'.

related.en: a matter; something to do (events, not objects)

meaning: child; kid; one's son or daughter

senses.en: child; kid (a young person)
one's child, son or daughter, at any age

measure.note: 一个孩子; 两个孩子

examples.en: Do you have kids?
examples.analysis: 孩子 here means 'children of your own': 有孩子 is the standard way to ask whether someone is a parent, common in small talk. Answer 有 or 没有. No plural form is needed: 孩子 covers one child or several.

examples.en: My kid is six this year.
examples.analysis: 我孩子 'my child', with no 的, as with other family words. Age needs no verb: 孩子 + 六岁. The final 了 marks the new state, 'has turned six'.

examples.zh: 孩子生病了，我今天不去上班了。
examples.en: My kid's sick, so I'm not going in to work today.
examples.analysis: 孩子 with no 'my': the listener knows whose child it is, so it is left out. 生病了 'has fallen ill' is the new situation; 不去…了 'not going after all' is the change of plan it causes.

related.en: kid; more casual, mostly for young children

hook: 孩 = 子 'child' + 亥 hài for the sound.

meaning: to get up; after a verb: up, or 'start to'

senses.en: to get up (out of bed); to stand up
after a verb: upward (拿起来 'pick up', 站起来 'stand up')
after a verb or adjective: start and keep going (冷起来 'turn cold')

examples.en: Get up, it's already eight!
examples.analysis: 起来 is the main verb, 'get up', here out of bed. 快 + verb pushes the listener: 'hurry and…'. 都…了 = 'already', with a note of complaint. 起床 is only 'get out of bed'; 起来 also covers standing up from a chair.

examples.zh: 天气冷起来了，多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It's turning cold, so put on more layers.
examples.analysis: After an adjective, 起来 means 'start to be, and keep on': 冷起来了 'has started getting cold'. 冷了 would just state the change. 多 + verb + 一点儿 = 'do a bit more of it': wear more.

examples.zh: 这东西太重了，我拿不起来。
examples.en: This thing is too heavy. I can't lift it.
examples.analysis: 拿起来 = 'pick up, lift': 起来 adds the upward direction to 拿. Putting 不 between the verb and 起来 says it can't be done: 拿不起来 'can't lift it'. 拿得起来 would be 'can lift it'.

collocations.en: to look, seem (看起来很累 'looks tired')

related.en: to get out of bed (only that)

meaning: these; these ones

senses.en: these, straight before a noun (这些人); in speech often zhèixiē
these ones; these things (on its own)

examples.en: Whose are these?
examples.analysis: 这些 stands alone as the subject, 'these (things)'. 谁的 = 'whose', the same 的 as in 我的 'mine'. Point at a pile of bags or a set of keys and this is the question; for a single item, ask 这是谁的？

examples.en: All these dishes are delicious.
examples.analysis: 这些 goes straight before the noun with no measure word in between, unlike 这个菜 'this dish'. 都 'all' points back to the plural subject 这些菜: every one of them is good.

examples.en: I don't want these things anymore.
examples.analysis: 这些东西 is the object moved to the front as the topic: 'these things, I don't want them'. 不要了 with 了 marks a change: you wanted them before, now you don't. Useful when clearing out a room or handing items back in a shop.

meaning: two (before a measure word); both; a couple of

senses.en: two, before a measure word: 两个, 两点, 两天
the two; both (你们两个 'you two')
a couple of; a few (说两句 'say a few words')

examples.en: I'll have two buns.
examples.analysis: 两 + measure word + noun: 两个包子 'two buns'. Before a measure word, Mandarin uses 两 for 'two'; 二个 is not standard. 二 is for counting (一, 二, 三), inside 十二 and 二十, and in 第二 'second'.

examples.en: Let's meet at two this afternoon.
examples.analysis: Clock time follows the same rule: 两点 'two o'clock', since 点 works like a measure word. The time goes before the verb: 下午两点 + 见. 吧 makes it a suggestion. 十二点 keeps 二 because it sits inside 十二.

examples.en: You two, off to bed now!
examples.analysis: 你们两个 = 'you two': a pronoun + 两个 names exactly the pair you mean, a common way to address two people. 快去 + verb = 'go and do it, quickly', a parent's command.

collocations.en: two days; a couple of days

related.en: two, in counting and inside numbers (十二, 第二)
two (people); a spoken merge of 两个: 我们俩

meaning: wrong; mistaken; a mistake, a fault

senses.en: wrong; incorrect (你错了 'you're wrong')
after a verb: do it wrong (说错, 写错, 坐错车)
fault; mistake (我的错 'my fault')

examples.en: We're on the wrong bus!
examples.analysis: Verb + 错 = 'do it wrong': 坐错车 'take the wrong bus (or train)'. 错 comes right after the verb, before the object. 了 marks that it has already happened. Same pattern: 走错 'go the wrong way', 拿错 'take the wrong one'.

examples.en: Did I write it wrong?
examples.analysis: 写错 = 'write it incorrectly', verb + 错 again. 是不是 before the verb asks 'is it the case that…?': you suspect a mistake and want it confirmed. Handy when you have filled in a form or written a character and are not sure it is right.

examples.en: It's my fault. Don't be angry.
examples.analysis: Here 错 is a noun, 'fault': 我的错 'my fault', with owner + 的 before it like any noun. 别 + verb = 'don't'. The same frame gives 不是你的错 'it's not your fault'.

related.en: wrong; not right (a stand-alone reply: 不对! 'That's not right!'; unlike 错, not a verb ending as in 说错, nor a noun as in 我的错)

meaning: there's still; there's more; also, one more thing

senses.en: there is still; still have (还有时间 'there's still time')
also; and; one more thing (adding a point)

examples.en: Are there any buns left?
examples.analysis: 还有 = 还 'still' + 有 'have': 'is there any left?'. At a food stall late in the day, this asks whether they've sold out. The answer is 有 or 没有了 'none left'.

examples.en: Two more days and then it's the holidays.
examples.analysis: 还有 + a stretch of time + 就…了 = 'only X left until…'. 还有两天 counts what remains; 就 'then' ties it to the event; 就…了 marks it as coming soon. Swap in 一个星期 'a week' or 十分钟 'ten minutes'.

examples.en: Also, there's a meeting at eight tomorrow.
examples.analysis: At the start of a sentence, followed by a pause, 还有 adds one more point: 'also; oh, and'. It is how you tack a reminder onto the end of a talk or a phone call. Time comes before the verb: 明天八点 + 开会.

meaning: small; little; young, younger

senses.en: small; little (size)
young; younger (他还小 'he's still little'; 小两岁 'two years younger')

examples.zh: 这杯子太小了，有大一点儿的吗？
examples.en: This cup's too small. Do you have a bigger one?
examples.analysis: 太 + 小 + 了 = 'too small'; the 了 belongs to the 太…了 frame. Then 大 + 一点儿 = 'a bit bigger', and 的 stands in for 杯子: 'a bigger one'. Swap the noun and it works for shoes, rooms or clothes.

examples.en: I'm two years younger than him.
examples.analysis: With age, 小 means 'younger'. Comparison order: A + 比 + B + adjective + amount. The amount 两岁 comes after the adjective, the reverse of English 'two years younger'. 大 gives 'older': 他比我大两岁.

examples.en: He's still little; he can't talk yet.
examples.analysis: 小 as a predicate needs no 'is': 他 + 还 'still' + 小 = 'he's still young'. Then 还不会 = 'can't yet', 会 being a learned skill. Said of a baby; of an older child who misbehaves, 他还小 is also a common excuse.

related.en: few; little in amount (小 is size, 少 is quantity)

meaning: middle; medium; among, in; China (in 中国, 中文)

senses.en: middle; medium (大、中、小 'large, medium, small')
among; in (after a group: 我们中 'among us'); a bit formal
China; Chinese, in compounds: 中国, 中文

examples.zh: 你要大杯、中杯还是小杯？
examples.en: Would you like a large, a medium or a small?
examples.analysis: 中 is the middle size in the set 大 / 中 / 小. In coffee and tea shops the size goes straight onto the measure word: 大杯, 中杯, 小杯. 还是 'or' offers the choice in a question.

examples.zh: 这个太大了，有中号的吗？
examples.en: This one's too big. Do you have a medium?
examples.analysis: 中号 = 'medium size', the label in clothes shops: 大号, 中号, 小号. 中号 + 的 stands in for the noun: 中号的 'a medium one'. 太大了 = 'too big'. Swap in 小号的 to ask for a small.

examples.en: Of the three of us, he's the tallest.
examples.analysis: After a group, 中 means 'among, out of': 我们三个人中 'among the three of us'. It sounds slightly formal; casual talk more often says 我们三个人里. 最 + adjective = 'the most', so 最高 'tallest'.

related.en: the middle; between (the everyday word for position)

meaning: to be called; to call (someone); to tell someone to do

senses.en: to be called; to call by a name (我叫…, 叫我小王)
to call someone over; to tell someone to do something
to order; to call for (叫车 'call a cab')

examples.en: What's your child's name?
examples.analysis: 叫 + name = 'be called'. 什么名字 'what name' sits exactly where the answer will go: 他叫小明. 你孩子 'your child' drops 的, as family words often do. A natural follow-up to 你有孩子吗？

examples.en: Mom says to come home for dinner.
examples.analysis: 叫 + person + action = 'tell someone to do something': 叫你回家吃饭. The person told (你) is both the object of 叫 and the one who acts. A sibling passing on a message would say exactly this.

examples.en: Just call me Xiao Wang.
examples.analysis: 叫 + person + name = 'call someone by a name': 叫我小王. 就行 'that'll do' makes it easygoing: you are offering your informal name. 小 + surname is a friendly name for someone younger.

related.en: to be surnamed (我姓王 'my surname is Wang')

meaning: to wait; to wait for

senses.en: to wait; to wait for (等我 'wait for me')
等 + event + 再: wait until …, then … (等他来了再吃)

examples.en: Wait for me a sec!
examples.analysis: 等 + person + 一下儿 = 'wait for someone a moment'. The person waited for comes straight after 等, with no word for 'for'. 一下儿 softens it to 'just a moment'; many southern speakers say 等我一下, without 儿.

examples.en: I've been waiting for you for ages!
examples.analysis: 等你 = 'wait for you'. 半天 here is not literally half a day: in speech it means 'a long while'. 都…了 = 'already', the speaker's complaint. The length of the wait comes after 等你.

examples.en: Don't wait for me. Go ahead and eat.
examples.analysis: 别 + 等我 + 了 = 'stop waiting for me', with 了 marking the change of plan. 先 'first' + 吃吧 = 'go ahead and eat (before I get there)'. A text you send when you're running late.

meaning: together; (in) the same place; altogether

senses.en: together (跟 + person + 一起 + verb 'do it with someone')
the same place (在一起 'together, in one place')
altogether; in total (一起多少钱 'how much in all')

examples.en: Let's go together.
examples.analysis: 一起 works as an adverb, so it sits before the verb: 一起 + 走. 我们…吧 makes it a suggestion, 'let's'. You might say it at the end of the workday or at the door of a restaurant.

examples.zh: 我今天不跟你们一起去了。
examples.en: I'm not going with you guys today after all.
examples.analysis: 跟 + person + 一起 + verb = 'do something with someone'. 不 goes before the whole 跟 phrase, not right before 去. The final 了 marks a change of plan: you were going, now you're not.

examples.en: How much for all of these?
examples.analysis: Here 一起 means 'all together, in total': you hand over several items and ask for one price. 多少钱 'how much money' is the price question. 一共 means the same and is a little more standard.

meaning: to take; to hold; to carry; to fetch

senses.en: to take; to pick up; to hold in the hand
to go and get; to fetch (去拿 'go and get')

examples.en: Here, take it. It's for you.
examples.analysis: 拿着 = 'take it and hold on to it': 着 marks keeping hold, so this is what you say while handing something over. 给你的 = 'for you', with 的 standing in for the gift. Often repeated when the other person politely refuses.

examples.en: I'm going to get some water. Do you want some?
examples.analysis: 去 + 拿 = 'go and get': the first verb says you move, the second what you do there. 拿水 'fetch water' needs no measure word. 你要吗 offers to bring the listener some too.

examples.en: Don't take my phone!
examples.analysis: 别 + 拿 = 'don't take'. 拿 is the everyday verb for taking something in your hand, from picking it up to carrying it off. A typical line to a child or a friend who grabs your phone.

related.en: to bring along; to carry with you

meaning: to help; to do something for someone

senses.en: to help (someone): 帮我 'help me'
帮 + person + verb: do something for someone (帮你拿 'carry it for you')

examples.en: Could you give me a hand for a second?
examples.analysis: 帮 + person = 'help someone'. 一下儿 makes the favor sound small and quick, which keeps the request polite. 能…吗 = 'can you…?'. A standard way to ask a colleague or a passer-by for help.

examples.en: Let me carry that for you.
examples.analysis: 帮 + person + verb = 'do it for someone': 帮你拿 'carry it for you'. Unlike English 'help you carry', 帮你拿 usually means you take over the whole job. 吧 makes it an offer.

examples.en: Thanks for helping me find my wallet!
examples.analysis: 谢谢你 + what they did: the whole favor 帮我找到钱包 follows directly, with no word for 'for'. 找到 = 'find' (look + succeed); 找钱包 alone would only be 'look for the wallet'.

collocations.en: to help; to do a favor

related.en: to help; takes no direct object (请帮忙, 帮我一个忙)

meaning: to hit; (with set objects) to make a call, take a taxi, play ball

senses.en: to make, do, play, with set objects: 打电话 'phone', 打车 'take a taxi', 打球 'play ball'
to hit; to beat; to strike

examples.zh: 我一会儿给你打个电话。
examples.en: I'll give you a call in a bit.
examples.analysis: 打电话 'make a phone call', with 个 slipped in between to make it casual: 打个电话 'give a call'. 给 + person comes before the verb to say who you call. 一会儿 'in a moment' also sits before the verb.

examples.en: It's too late. Let's get a taxi.
examples.analysis: 打车 = 'take a taxi', with 个 in between as in 打个电话. 打 here has nothing to do with hitting; it takes its meaning from the object. 太…了 = 'too…'; 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.en: Don't hit your little brother!
examples.analysis: Here 打 has its basic meaning, 'hit'. 别 + verb = 'don't', a common line from a parent. 你弟弟 'your younger brother' needs no 的, as with other family words.

related.en: to play; to have fun (the general word; most ball games take 打, as in 打球)

meaning: to love; to love doing; to tend to

senses.en: to love (a person, a place)
爱 + verb: to love doing; to enjoy (爱吃 'love eating')
爱 + verb: to tend to; to … easily (爱生病 'get ill easily')

examples.en: Mom, I love you!
examples.analysis: 爱 is the main verb: 我 + 爱 + 你, the same order as in English. 爱 is the strong 'love', natural for a parent, a child or a partner; 喜欢 is the everyday 'like'.

examples.en: He's not much of a talker.
examples.analysis: 爱 + verb = 'like to do', and with 不 it describes a habit: 不爱说话 'quiet, not chatty'. It describes the person's character, not a refusal to talk right now.

examples.zh: 我儿子身体不好，爱生病。
examples.en: My son isn't very healthy; he gets sick easily.
examples.analysis: 爱 + verb can mean 'tend to', even for things nobody wants: 爱生病 'often falls ill'. 身体不好 'in poor health' describes a weak constitution. The subject 我儿子 carries over into the second clause.

meaning: time (free time; an amount of time; a point in time)

senses.en: (free) time: 有时间 'be free'
time as an amount or a point (时间不早了 'it's getting late')

measure.note: 一段时间 'a period of time'

examples.en: Are you free tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 有时间 'have time' = 'be free', the usual way to check someone's availability before an invitation. 明天 'tomorrow' sits before the verb. Answer 有 or 没有, or 明天不行 'tomorrow's no good'.

examples.zh: 我现在没时间，晚上说吧。
examples.en: I don't have time right now. Let's talk tonight.
examples.analysis: 没时间 = 'no time', with 没, not 不, because it negates 有. 晚上说吧 'let's talk this evening' puts the conversation off politely; 吧 keeps it friendly.

examples.zh: 时间不早了，我们回家吧。
examples.en: It's getting late. Let's go home.
examples.analysis: 时间不早了 is a set way to say 'it's getting late', literally 'the time is no longer early'. 不 + adjective + 了 marks the change. It also politely signals that you want to end a visit or a meeting.
